concepts.why: The patient presented with quadriplegia, complete sensory loss, and spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis, which are all consistent with a cervical spinal cord injury.
The patient fell out of bed, which is a traumatic event, and presented with quadriplegia and spinal cord compression, consistent with a traumatic spinal cord injury.
The patient presented with absent rectal tone, urinary and stool incontinence, and reduced diffusion in the spinal cord white matter, which are all consistent with an acute spinal cord injury.
The patient presented with reduced diffusion in the spinal cord white matter at the level of C5 and C6, which is consistent with a C5-C6 spinal cord injury.
It explains the patient's low body temperature of 33.1°C.
It explains the reduced diffusion in the spinal cord white matter and the hypointense signal of the central gray matter.
